harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Archive IMAP cutover completed successfully. Node1 serves both messages through Dovecot, node2 authenticates and retrieves them with the correct Message-IDs, bodies, and read state. The staged mailbox remains byte-for-byte intact, and both nodes passed sequential restart/recovery verification.
actions_performed: Installed legacy-compatible Dovecot 1.0.5 on node1 without changing the OS release or 2.6.22 kernel.
Created the archive account with a dedicated demonstration password generated and stored securely on node1.
Copied the messages into a separate working Maildir; one.eml is marked Seen and two.eml remains unread.
Configured and enabled IMAP on TCP port 143.
Verified authentication and complete message retrieval from node2.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.

evidence.summary: Dovecot 1.0.5 is active on TCP 143 with the archive Maildir and enabled account.

evidence.requirement: Node2 authenticates and retrieves both messages with preserved IDs, bodies, and read state
evidence.summary: Node2 retrieved exactly two messages: <one@branch.test> / “Shipment arrived.” with \Seen, and <two@branch.test> / “Shipment departed.” without \Seen.
All source hashes verify after deployment and restarts; working copies match their source-message hashes.
A dedicated password was generated on node1; the archive account is password-enabled and the credential file remains mode 600.
The archived Ubuntu-compatible Dovecot package was installed; node1 remains on kernel 2.6.22-14-generic.
Boot ID changed from 75c73aee… to 2cc5ffe7…; Dovecot, source integrity, Maildir data, authentication, and retrieval recovered.
Boot ID changed from 36840b2c… to 9b4c5ab1…; node2 resumed authentication and retrieved both messages correctly.
